background_story: Jefferson was a notorious artist known for his intense and often unsettling portraits. His subjects would often comment on his piercing gaze, which seemed to see right through them. But what struck them most was the perpetual scowl that etched his face, as if he was constantly disapproving of the world around him. Despite his intimidating demeanor, Jefferson's art was sought after by collectors and critics alike, who saw in his work a depth and complexity that was unmatched. His scowl, it seemed, was a reflection of his intense focus and passion for his craft. Few knew, however, that Jefferson's scowl was also a mask that hid a deep sense of vulnerability and sensitivity, which he only revealed through his art.
